question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=3{z}^{2}+4z-5.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}z}=6z+4\,⟹\,\text{d}u=(6z+4)\,\text{d}z.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (6z+4){e}^{3{z}^{2}+4z-5}\,\text{d}z & =\int {e}^{3{z}^{2}+4z-5}\cdot (6z+4)\text{d}z \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & ={e}^{3{z}^{2}+4z-5}+C\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=3{t}^{2}-4.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t}=6t\,⟹\,\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u=t\,\text{d}t.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{3{t}^{2}-4}\,\text{d}t & =\int {e}^{3{t}^{2}-4}\cdot t\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int {e}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\int {e}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot {e}^{u}+C \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3{t}^{2}-4}}{6}+C.\end{aligned}
$$
